769.t: El Morocco in 1950 and the band lineup
769.s: Nick Gagliano gets the band steady work at El Morocco on Bourbon and Iberville with Talbot, Slow Drag, Purnell, Lewis, Marrero and Jim Robinson.
769.q: Well we had Talbot, Slow Drag, Elton Pornell, George Lewis, Lawrence Moreira and myself. That was the old regular lineup.

769.t: Joining George Lewis and the road to national fame
769.s: Drag recommended him to George Lewis. They played Manny's, got Nick as manager, moved to El Morocco (c. 1949-50), and Reverend Kershaw and Dr. Ball took them to Cincinnati, Los Angeles and beyond.
769.ch: Early bands and joining George Lewis
769.q: And we had a crippled fellow on the clarinet. I can't think of his name now. He's dead. And sometimes we have George Lewis and drag. Well, the piano player, I didn't know his name. Then we had another fellow by the name of Alfred used to play sax with us sometime when we couldn't get clarinet.…

178.t: Moves between the Happy Land and the Melody Inn
178.s: Ferbos went to Happy Land with Idru Coleman and others, returned to Dejan, and Andrew Morgan replaced Dejan at Happy Land.
178.ch: Happy Land, sidemen and other bands
178.q: Well that's when I went to the Happy Land and then. You went to the Happy Land and then. Again, I went back to the Happy Land.

899.t: Harmony Inn, slowing down around 1950, no street parades
899.s: He played three nights a week at the Harmony Inn in the 1940s, slowed down around 1950, and says all his jobs were sit-in jobs, not parades.
899.q: I have a set of drums and everything. I have a good set of drums. And, well I slacked down say around 1949 I think. Or 1950. Yeah, around 1950. It ain't too far back. No, no. You don't lose too much practice.

891.t: Playing with George Lewis and Cuckoo
891.s: He worked with George Lewis before Herbert Morand and Cuckoo, until his own side band and Lewis's change of players.
891.q: You see, I worked with George back at Benefit and St. Rock, and I had my band on the side, you see. At that time, I couldn't make it with George, because I had my little side band, you see. And we worked right there a good while, but after that, I had jobs, that well, uh, um, Loran, he's got my…

799.t: Leading a band at Pete Herman's
799.s: He led a five-piece band at Pete Herman's, hired Charlie Stowe, left for the shipyard, then took the St. Charles Theater job.
799.q: Well, the first, I worked at Pete Herman three different times. The first time when I went to New York he wanted me to put a band in his place and I told him I was all set to go to New York. But when I came back, 1940, I had a band in Pete Herman's and when the war came out I left to go to work in…

632.t: Herb Moran at the Rainbow Bar and the Lewis band at El Morocco
632.s: Journal entries from May 1950 on Moran's group, the record shop band and the Lewis El Morocco opening.

392.t: The El Moraco and a visiting English group
392.s: George Lewis once played the El Moraco; later a group from England played there.
392.ch: Later years and the club's fate
392.q: And what other bands they had, I don't know, but, uh, I see they were, they wind up with girl shows and, uh, with this crusading discraternity that looked down his nose on girl shows and girl activities. They were closed up. And, uh, so they didn't have a real girl shows or Dixieland either. But…

896.t: Guitar years with Kid Thomas at Speck's and Foster Lewis
896.s: After taking up guitar he played small outfits, then two or three years with Kid Thomas at Speck's, an eleven-piece band during wartime.
896.q: After I took up the guitar? Mm-hmm. After I took up the guitar, well, I played with different outfits. Oh, yeah. Just small outfits, you know. Nothing much to talk about.

308.t: Filling in at the Mardi Gras Lounge; how the Paddock mixed bands
308.s: Substituting for Lewis's men, trying banjoists, and the Paddock manager shuffling groups; many musicians refused to play there.
308.q: MacNeil Bro. MacNeil Bro got Bro, that's right. Then we tried Ache on banjo. Oh, yeah. He had Ache in there a while. And Ache, he left and then we got George Guino.
